mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% triggers a negative signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as higher unemployment reduces consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the housing starts series (HOUST) and the retail sales series (RSAFS) both exhibit a 3-month moving average increase of over 5%, it signals a strong demand environment that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS does not lead to significantly higher 60-day forward returns compared to periods without this joint increase (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) by more than 2% over a 6-month period signals a supply chain disruption that negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods following a 2% decline in INDPRO over 6 months, compared to other periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) jointly predict S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, with higher FEDFUNDS and lower CPIAUCSL indicating a positive signal.
failure_condition: The joint behavior of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL does not lead to significantly higher 5-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS is high and CPIAUCSL is low, compared to other conditions (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over a 3-month period signals a strong labor market that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods following a 200,000 increase in PAYEMS over 3 months, compared to other periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The GDP series (GDPC1) and the housing starts series (HOUST) jointly predict S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, with higher GDPC1 and HOUST indicating a positive signal.
failure_condition: The joint increase in GDPC1 and HOUST does not lead to significantly higher 60-day forward returns compared to periods without this joint increase (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the capacity utilization rate (not available in the given catalog, using INDPRO as a proxy) by more than 5% over a 6-month period signals a supply chain disruption that negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods following a 5% decline in INDPRO over 6 months, compared to other periods (t-test p > 0.05).
